scope_choices: Automated model review, not independent human verification, replication, clinical validation or authorization.
All nine text pages and earlier API image-review notes were supplied. Earlier page calls received images; this synthesis did not inspect images directly.
Source path/hash are supplied provenance, not recomputed or checked on disk. No external bibliographic, repository or release check was performed.
All 128 feature definitions received dispositions, with a separate endpoint-calibration scope. Programmatic schema/reference/KG validation was not executed.
The model ID denotes the reported experimental configuration, not an exact shared weights artifact. Task-specific checkpoint identities and exact DINOv2 variant are unreported.
Learned procedural endpoint dynamics are implemented, but future-state fidelity results and a separate L0 representation evaluation are not reported. Demonstrated L-level remains unknown.
Direct K-step endpoint supervision is not recursive rollout or traversal-based multi-step training. Legacy BW uses a broader target-based rule.
Robot timestep t, endpoint gap K, history L, window H and generative transport tau are distinct. No physical window duration or reciprocal latency was calculated.
Alarm scoring requires a completed observed window. Failure-onset-relative delay, early warning, live response and harm prevention are not reported.
Inverse-base distance is a nonconformity score, not an established clinical failure probability or exact conditional log likelihood.
Episode-maximum conformal alarm calibration is not calibration of endpoint probabilities or generated future-state trajectories. Aleatoric/epistemic components are not separated.
Nominal alpha=0.05 differs from observed FAR 10.0% fixed and 1.3% wrist. No uncertainty-qualified acceptance analysis establishes a general calibration pass/fail.
Fixed and wrist detectors are independent; joint guarantees, alarm fusion and clinical/camera/policy transfer are not established.
Expert-demonstration counts, command dimensions/units/frames, operator/session/material dependence, model size, solver settings and training compute are insufficiently reported.
The same evaluation episodes are used across K settings; independence of architecture/horizon selection is unreported.
Different simulated and physical tasks do not establish matched sim-to-real agreement. Physical material is not classified as human, animal, ex-vivo or a specific phantom type without provenance.
Held-out robot executions support R1, not R2 actual human/clinical validation. Expert teleoperation is not a human reader/use evaluation.
Fault challenges reveal missed detections and false alarms but do not establish exhaustive hazard coverage, a fully specified injection protocol or a security threat model.
Pooled rates mix task sample sizes. Detector comparisons do not uniformly match observed FAR; fixed WM-NC improves FDR over fixed RND while also having higher FAR.
The independently imitation-trained ACT host does not establish WM-coupled control, detector autonomy or evaluated intervention utility.
Hard guards, abstention, stop, escalation, privacy/security controls, ethics documentation and operational lifecycle governance remain insufficiently reported.
Assets are promised upon acceptance; actual accessibility, separate licenses and independent reproduction are not established.
References [1]–[31] were read as bibliography/context, not retrieved primary studies. Their planning, human-study and clinical capabilities are not inherited.
Earlier image notes contain chunk-local unavailable-page caveats; those do not describe the combined nine-page input.
Approximate graph readings and reviewer arithmetic in earlier notes are not promoted to source-reported metrics. Table paraphrases rely on the supplied prior image transcription plus full text.
